t: You're facing Chartered Accountants' Hall, at 1 Moorgate Place in the City of London. It's the headquarters of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, and it's Grade Two star listed. It's counted among the richest examples of late Victorian architecture in the City, and it's praised for how smoothly its sculpture is woven into the building. John Belcher, who also served as president of the Royal Institute of British Architects, designed it, with John James Joass, a Scottish architect born in Dingwall. Sir William Whitfield, an architect and town planner, is also credited with its design.
